title: AIDA implementation tests-frozen record
description: What `tests-freeze` verified and froze for one unit, at <task folder>/implementation/tests-<unit_id>.json (ideal/implementation.md, 'The split between the script and the model'). The model that writes a test chooses the level, writes the file, and runs it; this record is the script's own half, verifying what came back rather than writing or judging a test itself. One record per unit. Taken once per commit: a second `tests-freeze` run for this unit at the same commit and the same inputs leaves this file untouched, and a run at a different commit refuses rather than overwrite it, naming both commits. Plain JSON, no fences, no markdown. A field present in a real record but absent from this schema's `properties` is a defect in the schema, not a value to silently accept, which is why `additionalProperties` is false.

schemaVersion.description: The shape this file was written in, the same field every other AIDA record carries.

takenAt.description: The UTC date this record was written, YYYY-MM-DD. Set by the script, never typed. Left unchanged by a rerun at the same commit whose inputs did not change, the same as the rest of this file: that rerun leaves the file byte-identical rather than only updating this one field.

unit.description: The work order id this record belongs to, the same id `tests-brief` was given and the file's own basename encodes (tests-<unit_id>.json). Joined on, never re-minted.

commit.description: The commit the test files in `rows` are in: the one `tests-freeze` made from them, on the task branch, or HEAD when they were already committed. Read fresh from the code repository rather than from the ledger's own startedFrom: unlike a baseline, which is pinned to the commit the whole build began from, a unit's own tests may be frozen after other units have already advanced the branch. A second run for this unit at a different commit refuses rather than overwrite this field.

testGlobs.description: The `--test-glob` patterns this run was given, copied verbatim. They come from the framework's own `implement` recipe declaration, resolved by the skill and pinned here rather than fetched again; every `--test` path in `rows` matched at least one of them, which is the check that keeps a test written outside the framework's own pattern from being protected by anything later.

rows.description: One entry per machine-verified criterion a `--test` named, one per person-verified criterion the unit serves or owns, and one for the unit's own doneWhen when a `--test` proves it. A machine-verified criterion the unit only serves and no test names gets no row: its proof lives with the order that owns it (live-run row 59). A criterion the unit neither serves nor owns never gets a row, whatever a `--test` might have claimed for it: that claim is refused before this file is ever written. Never empty when `proof` is tests: a record with no row is refused (exit 74). When `proof` is gate the unit takes no `--test`, so this holds only the checklist rows of its person-verified criteria, and may be empty.

support.description: The files the test author wrote beside the tests and the tests stand on: a base class, a fixture. Each came from one `--support` flag, is hashed here and committed in the same commit as the tests, so the frozen-tests check reads it as it reads a test and hooks/deny-frozen-test-writes.sh guards it the same way. Refused before this file is written when the path is missing (exit 89) or when a `testGlobs` pattern matches it, because that file is a test and belongs on `--test` (exit 89). Empty when the freeze was given no `--support`. Absent on a record written before this field existed, which reads as empty (live-run row 90).

proof.description: Copied from the frozen work order. `gate` says this unit froze no test on purpose: its deliverable is exported configuration, and its build runs the implement recipe's `## Configuration gate` lines as its own check in place of order-tests (live-run row 65). `record` says the same for a unit whose deliverable is a document in the task folder: no test, `rows` empty unless a person-verified criterion adds a checklist, and the one row it owes, the done-when judgement from `--row <unit_id>=...`, sits on the ledger's order entry (nyc defect 17). Absent on a record written before this field existed, which reads as tests.

path.description: Where the support file lives, relative to the project's own codePath, never absolute, for the same reason a test's `path` is. Resolved and refused (exit 36) the same way when it names something outside codePath.

sha256.description: sha256 over the whole file at `path`, computed at freeze, the same hash a test carries. A support file whose hash no longer matches reads frozen-tests unmet, the same as a changed test.

criterion.description: The criterion id, minted by scope in alignment.json and copied into the frozen snapshot. Joined on, never renamed. Null on the one row that proves the unit's own doneWhen rather than a criterion, which `provesDoneWhen` marks.

provesDoneWhen.description: Present, and true, only on the row whose tests prove the unit's own doneWhen: the tests a `--test` flag named with the unit's id in place of a criterion id. A supporting order serves criteria it cannot observe, because the thing they observe is built by their owner later, so its tests are frozen against what the order itself said it would make true (ideal/design.md, 'An order that owns nothing is a supporting order'). At most one such row per record; `kind` stays `machine` so every reader that selects machine rows for their tests runs and hashes these the same as a criterion's. Judged at the checkpoint against the doneWhen text, and that judgement sits on the order's own ledger entry as `doneWhenJudgement`.

kind.description: Copied from this criterion's own frozen `verifiedBy`, so a reader of this file never has to look the criterion back up to know which of `tests` or `checklist` it carries.

tests.description: Present only when `kind` is `machine`. Every `--test` this run was given that named this criterion, however many; a test naming several criteria appears once in each criterion's own row. On the doneWhen row, every `--test` that named the unit's id. Never empty when present, because a machine row is written only for a criterion or a doneWhen at least one test named.

checklist.description: Present only when `kind` is `person`: the verification text from this criterion's own `--checklist` row, copied rather than summarised, because a person judging this criterion later reads exactly what the recipe was asked to confirm.

path.description: Where the test lives, relative to the project's own codePath, never absolute: a frozen path must still mean the same file once the checkout moves, the same reason baseline.json's own `scope` field is repository-relative. A `--test` flag may name the file by an absolute path or one already relative to codePath; either is resolved against codePath and refused (exit 36) when it names something outside it, before this file is ever written. Checked to exist on disk and, in this relative form, to match one of `testGlobs`.

name.description: The test's own name, as the `--test` flag named it. Checked to carry, at its own end, the criterion id (or ids, chained from the right) it claims, or the unit's own id on the doneWhen row, so a person or a later step can tell what a test is meant to prove without opening the file.

sha256.description: sha256 over the whole file at `path`, computed at freeze. This is the freeze itself: nothing else in the plugin may change a file whose hash is recorded here. A file naming several tests carries the same hash in each of its tests' own entries, since the hash covers the file, not one test inside it.

red.description: What running this test printed before the code existed, copied verbatim from the file the `--red` flag pointed at. Checked to hold one of the assertion markers the test-execution recipe declares under `failure_signal`, or a line its suite row's `failure_line` names (exit 80); `redSignal` says which. A run that never reached a test, a harness error included, is refused before this file is written, except for the order that creates the unit, whose first run can only stop there (`redSignal: harness-new-unit`). Never empty and never synthesised: a test with neither a red run nor a `locksIn` reason is refused before this file is written (exit 33), and a `--green-on-arrival` report stops the whole step rather than being recorded here (exit 34), because a test proving nothing before the code exists proves nothing after it either. Absent only when `locksIn` is present.

redSignal.description: Present whenever `red` is. How `tests-freeze` read the red file as a failed test: `assertion`, it holds a marker the recipe's `failure_signal.assertion` declares; `failure-line`, a line matches the suite row's `failure_line` selector, which also covers a test that errored in its own body while another failed, because PHPUnit then prints ERRORS! and no FAILURES!; `harness-new-unit`, it holds the `failure_signal.harness` marker and no assertion marker, and the freeze accepted it because this order creates the unit: an owned file matches a glob under the implement recipe's `## Unit declaration`. A person re-reading the freeze should know this red proved the harness stopped before the unit existed, though a test that ran may also have failed in it; `unchecked`, the recipes handed over declare neither a usable marker nor a selector, so only the non-empty check ran, and the freeze said so in one summary line.

locksIn.description: Present when the test was green on its first run, after one correction, because code that already existed satisfies it: one sentence from the test author naming that code, copied from the `--locks-in` flag. The test then locks that behaviour in rather than driving new code, the outcome version 5's tdd-companion called ratified. The reviewer reads this reason with the diff, so the review brief says where it is.
